item.description: By Adesina Wahab Teachers of the International School, University of Lagos (ISL), on Wednesday began a work-to-rule action over delays in implementing a National Industrial Court judgment, payment of outstanding salary arrears and restoration of their names to the university’s payroll. The teachers are demanding the implementation of the court judgment, payment of outstanding Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Teaching Allowance (CONTTA) arrears and the 2024 arrears arising from the 25 per cent and 35 per cent salary adjustments. item.title: FUTATH mourns Fasoranti, describes him as dependable voice for justice, equity, federalism
item.description: — Says role in FUTA teaching hospital will be remembered – CMD By Dayo Johnson Akure The Federal University of Technology Akure Teaching Hospital (FUTATH) has mourned the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing him as a dependable voice for justice, equity, true federalism and good governance. The Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Teaching Hospital, Prof. Olusegun Ojo, in a statement he personally signed, condoled with the family of the elder statesman over his passage. The statement reads: “With heavy hearts but profound gratitude to God for an uncommon life of service, we commiserate with the immediate family of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the good people of Akure, Ondo State, and the entire nation over the passage of this revered elder statesman, who died yesterday at the old and ripe age of 100 years. “Pa Fasoranti was a teacher, school administrator, politician, pro-democracy activist, and a dependable voice for justice, equity, true federalism, and good governance. “As a former Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State and, for many years, the leader of Afenifere, he served with integrity, courage, and an enduring commitment to the progress of the Yoruba people and Nigeria. “Beyond public service, Baba was a visionary educationist whose legacy lives on through the schools he established, including Omolere Nursery and Primary School, Akure High School, and St. Frances’ Academy, Igoba. “He shaped generations of learners and demonstrated, throughout his life, that leadership is best measured by the opportunities one creates for others. “We particularly recall with deep appreciation his pivotal role in the actualisation of the FUTA Teaching Hospital, Akure. “His advocacy, credibility, fatherly intervention, and personal engagement with the Federal Government were instrumental in bringing the long-awaited teaching hospital to Akure. “This singular contribution will continue to strengthen medical education, healthcare delivery, and specialist care for the people of Ondo State and beyond. “Pa Fasoranti lived a full, purposeful, and impactful life. He was a bridge-builder, a defender of the voiceless, and a rare statesman whose counsel transcended politics. ” Though we mourn his physical departure, we take comfort in the enduring institutions, ideals, and lives he touched.” Prof. Ojo prayed for the family of the late Yoruba leader who died on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at his residence in Akure, the Ondo State capital. “We pray that God will grant his immediate family, Afenifere, and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said. The CMD prayed that “May his gentle soul find eternal rest, and may his legacy of service, education, justice, and nation-building continue to inspire present and future generations.” The post FUTATH mourns Fasoranti, describes him as dependable voice for justice, equity, federalism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta More than 100 students from several secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo areas of Ogun State were reportedly hospitalised on Wednesday following another suspected gas emission that left students and staff struggling to breathe, with some fainting. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students fainting and being rushed for medical attention as panic spread across the affected communities. The incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities calling on the state government to establish the source and prevent further exposure. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties. “The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and had to be rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close for the day at about 11 a.m. as the situation worsened. “Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day when the situation became frightening and unbearable. The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode,” the teacher added. The teacher said parents who heard about the incident rushed to their children’s schools to take them home amid fears for their safety. The teacher further claimed that similar emissions had occurred since April, sending hundreds of students to hospitals during previous incidents. “We are all worried about our health and the safety of our students. item.title: EFCC chairman, Mbah, Umahi to grace Enugu NUJ Press Week
item.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — The Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Ola Olukoyede; Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah; and the Minister of Works, David Umahi, are among the dignitaries expected at the grand finale of the 2026 Press Week of the Enugu State Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) on Wednesday. The event, scheduled to hold at the Lawrence Ugwuanyi Press Centre, Enugu, will feature discussions on responsible journalism, democratic development and the media’s role in the fight against corruption. Umahi will deliver the guest lecture, while Olukoyede will give the keynote address at the ceremony, which is expected to attract media professionals, government officials, political leaders, security chiefs and other stakeholders. In a statement signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the Press Week Organising Committee, Emma Ugwueze and Damian Duruiheoma, respectively, the committee said the topics were carefully selected to address critical issues affecting the country. It said Umahi and Olukoyede were chosen in recognition of their respective roles in public service, particularly the minister’s efforts in road infrastructure development and the EFCC chairman’s leadership of the country’s anti-corruption campaign. “While Engr. David Umahi, the Honourable Minister of Works, is making visible efforts towards the rehabilitation and revitalisation of several roads across the country, the EFCC Chairman, Olukoyede, has also introduced reforms aimed at strengthening the operations of the anti-graft commission,” the statement said. Umahi’s lecture will focus on the theme, “Strengthening Democracy Through Responsible Journalism: 2027 Polls in Focus,” while Olukoyede will speak on “The Role of the Media and Other Critical Stakeholders in Sustaining the Fight Against Corruption.” The former Enugu State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Chief Anthony Ani, SAN, will chair the event. Among those expected to receive awards are the Deputy National Chairman (South) of the All Progressives Congress, Dr Ben Nwoye; the Executive Director of the Projects Development Institute (PRODA), Enugu, Dr Peter Okwudilichukwu Ogbobe; and the Enugu State Commissioner of Police, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa. Others are the Commissioner representing Enugu State at the Federal Character Commission, Peter Eze; the General Manager of Rangers International Football Club, Amobi Ezeaku; and medical expert Dr Celestine Chijioke Ugwuoke, among other recipients. The grand finale will conclude a series of activities organised by the chapel to mark the 2026 Press Week. The programme commenced on Sunday, October 18, with a thanksgiving service at the Christian Victory Prayer Ministry, popularly known as Precious Church, in Enugu. The bill also provides for a Suicide Prevention Unit, national and state surveillance systems, 24-hour crisis helplines and mandatory training for health workers, law enforcement and correctional personnel. The bill drew support from several senators. Senator Dayo Faduyile, a medical doctor, noted that some survivors have subsequently died by suicide while in detention. The bill has been referred to the Committees on Health and on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for a public hearing. Nigeria’s human rights obligations The question is not solely one of health policy. Nigeria has accepted binding obligations that bear directly on it. UN Special Rapporteurs on the right to health and on torture have found the criminalisation of suicide attempts inconsistent with these obligations, noting that the detention of persons in acute distress may engage the prohibition of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. The World Health Organization identifies decriminalisation as a critical step towards the Sustainable Development Goal target of reducing suicide mortality by one third by 2030. Incarceration exacerbates psychological suffering, stripping individuals of their agency at their most vulnerable moment rather than providing therapeutic care. Distortion of public health data and interventions. Decriminalisation is a prerequisite for effective public health governance. When suicide attempts are illegal, official data severely underreports the true scale of the mental health crisis in Nigeria. Accurate data is essential to design targeted suicide prevention strategies, establish crisis helplines, train emergency responders, and allocate adequate health sector budgets. item.description: Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta said the club was “concerned” about the severity of an injury to winger Bukayo Saka after Wednesday’s pulsating 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich. item.title: Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Wednesday, directed aviation authorities to place 46 persons who had contact with the Ebola-infected person on a no-fly list for 21 days to prevent the possible spread of the virus. Keyamo, who also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports, said he had instructed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines about the development. He disclosed this on X, formerly Twitter, after holding a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate. The minister stated: “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge. He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest). “I have therefore directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development. I have also directed FAAN to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports. Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” Vanguard News The post Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Governor Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of the people of Kano State in the 2027 general election. According to him, the people of Kano will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf stated this on Wednesday while representing president Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa in Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying that the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. Governor Yusuf also revealed that many projects executed by President Tinubu had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that the people of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over. He insisted that Tinubu’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts. He added that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road project and the Zari-Hunkuyi road project. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. He added that some inherited projects had been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. According to Umahi, the Tinubu administration has completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects are ongoing in the region. He said the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. item.title: Real Madrid Rout Leipzig, Continue Perfect European Start
item.description: Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval. Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on. Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. Basiru said President Bola Tinubu had emphasised the need for politicians to accept both victory and defeat, adding that the APC had experienced losses in court cases and political contests but had moved on. “One of the things that our leader President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said is that anybody that wants that savour the joy of victory in a democracy must also be able to endure the pain when he loses. But in the case of Nigeria, it appears that the opposition only wants to win, they don’t want to lose. We have had our fair share of losses both in the court and in the political contests, and we have taken it, learn our lessons and moved on,” he said. item.title: US embassy staff, families ordered to leave Saudi Arabia
item.description: Washington has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. It came after a diplomatic source told AFP that “all American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy” in the Gulf kingdom. The source added that families of embassy staff had also been ordered to leave the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, all of which have been targeted by Iran during the Middle East war. US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott subsequently confirmed the order in a post on X, but said it applied to “non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only”. He linked the move to Houthi attacks on the country, including airports, saying “the safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority”. Saudi Arabia has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates. On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two. “The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others,” the ministry said in a statement. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones. In June, a four-year-old truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed, reviving the conflict that dates back to 2014.
